title: Underlying set sheaf of a constructible module sheaf
statement: Let X be a scheme and Lambda a finite commutative ring. If F is a constructible sheaf of Lambda-modules on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf], then forgetting its module structure to abelian groups and then to sets gives a constructible sheaf of sets [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. The same finite constructible locally closed stratification witnesses the conclusion; no Noetherian hypothesis on X is needed.

source.place: Tags 095E(3), 03RU and 09Z6: forgetting finite module trivializations in the partition argument

proof.text: Choose the finite constructible locally closed stratification and finite constant-module trivializations supplied by module constructibility. Copy the domains, immersions and topological stratification into Scheme.Stratification. Forget modules first to abelian groups and then to sets. Inverse image commutes with this composite forgetful functor: underlying sets preserve finite limits and filtered colimits, so they commute with the local equivalence relation construction of inverse image and sheafification. Restriction to an object is computed sectionwise and commutes with forgetting. Constant sheaves are locally constant functions with values in the coefficient object, so forgetting a constant module sheaf gives the constant set sheaf of the same underlying finite set. Apply these comparisons to each trivializing isomorphism to obtain local constancy of the set pullback to every stratum.

For each geometric point of a stratum choose a lift to a member of its jointly surjective etale trivializing cover. Restriction does not change its geometric stalk, and the stalk of a constant set sheaf is its constant value. The chosen finite module therefore supplies a finite set stalk. This proves finite local constancy on each stratum, hence constructibility of the underlying set sheaf. The empty scheme permits an empty partition, and the zero module has a singleton underlying set, so neither case needs an additional assumption.
